name: Apollo 11
short_status: Success: first crewed lunar landing, July 20, 1969, 20:17:40 UTC at Tranquility Base; crew returned to Earth July 24, 1969.
tagline: NASA · United States · Crewed landing · 1969 · The space race Success
stats: estimated live TV audience for the first step
retroreflector deployed, still in scientific use today

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 16 July 1969, 9:32 a.m. EDT (13:32 UTC), Kennedy Space Center Launch Pad 39A, Saturn V

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: Neil Armstrong (Commander), Michael Collins (Command Module Pilot), Buzz Aldrin (Lunar Module Pilot)

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 20 July 1969, 20:17:40 UTC, Mare Tranquillitatis, 0.67416 N, 23.47314 E

facts.label: Moonwalk
facts.value: One EVA of about 2.5 hours, ending 111 h 39 m mission elapsed time; crew stayed within about 300 feet of Eagle

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 24 July 1969, 12:50 p.m. EDT, Pacific Ocean, 13 miles from USS Hornet

facts.label: Mission duration
facts.value: 195 h 18 m 35 s, about 36 minutes longer than planned

facts.label: TV audience
facts.value: An estimated 650 million people watched Armstrong's first step

facts.label: Retroreflector legacy
facts.value: Apollo-era retroreflector data still used more than 50 years later (NASA, 2 Jan 2025); successor NGLR-1 delivered to the Moon in 2025

facts.label: Flag status
facts.value: LROC imaging shows flags standing at all Apollo sites except Apollo 11; Aldrin reported it was blown over by ascent engine exhaust

facts.label: Crew status
facts.value: Armstrong died 25 Aug 2012; Collins died 28 Apr 2021; Aldrin is the last living crew member (as of July 2026)

timeline: President Kennedy sets the national goal of a crewed lunar landing and safe return
Launch from Kennedy Space Center Pad 39A at 9:32 a.m. EDT (13:32 UTC)
Lunar orbit insertion, about 75 h 50 m after launch
Eagle lands at Tranquility Base, 20:17:40 UTC
Armstrong's first step at 10:56 p.m. EDT (02:56 UTC 21 Jul); one EVA of about 2.5 hours
Ascent from the Moon at 124 h 22 m mission elapsed time after 21 h 36 m on the surface; docking with Columbia at 128 h 3 m
Pacific splashdown at 12:50 p.m. EDT, 13 miles from USS Hornet; mission duration 195:18:35
LROC imaging confirms the Apollo 11 flag is no longer standing, as Aldrin reported
NGLR-1, the retroreflector program's successor instrument, lands via Blue Ghost; Grasse, Wettzell, and Apache Point record laser returns
